title: Schur's Theorem: Monochromatic Sum Solutions in Ramsey Theory
description: Proves Schur's Theorem (1916): for any r-coloring of positive integers, there exists a monochromatic solution to x + y = z. Derives from Ramsey's theorem via edge-coloring construction: color {i,j} by color of |j-i|, extract monochromatic triangle to get Schur triple. Proves Schur number lower bounds and S(2)=5. Imports Proofs.RamseysTheorem (1 axiom) + 4 own axioms = 5 total.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: 5 axioms total: 1 from Proofs.RamseysTheorem (ramsey_theorem) + 4 own (Schur number bounds).

overview.historicalContext: Schur (1916) proved the theorem using Ramsey theory. Schur numbers S(r) grow rapidly: S(1)=2, S(2)=5, S(3)=14, S(4)=45, S(5)=161.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Schur's theorem as a consequence of Ramsey's theorem.
overview.proofStrategy: Given r-coloring of [1,n], color edge {i,j} by color of |j-i|; Ramsey gives monochromatic triangle {a,b,c}; (b-a),(c-b),(c-a) form Schur triple.
keyInsights: **schurs_theorem**: Every finite coloring of positive integers contains a monochromatic Schur triple
**Assumptions**: 5 axioms total: 1 from Proofs.RamseysTheorem (ramsey_theorem) + 4 own (Schur number bounds).
